props.text: Use an agreement reference to connect this escrow to the job or invoice it covers. When creation succeeds, the sending wallet becomes the client.
Reference and URI limits count UTF-8 bytes; some characters use more than one byte.

Required: choose a reference such as invoice-2026-01. It must be unique for this client in this escrow contract, even after closure. Lookup uses the exact text, including case and spaces. The contract derives a separate agreement ID from the client address and reference.

props.title: Create and fund an escrow agreement

props.text: Set up an agreement that holds the client’s money while the contractor carries out the work. Choose the parties, amount, deadlines and terms, then create and fund it in one transaction.
This agreement has three roles: the client funds and reviews, the contractor accepts and submits work, and the arbitrator can decide who receives disputed funds.

Both addresses are required: 0x followed by 40 hexadecimal characters. Replace the all-zero placeholders. Client, contractor and arbitrator must differ; neither entered address may be this escrow contract.
The arbitrator has no on-chain acceptance step. Naming an arbitrator does not confirm they have agreed to arbitrate.
Enter the money to commit to this agreement. It is funded at creation and held in escrow rather than sent straight to the contractor.
Enter a positive amount. Creation locks this amount; transaction fees are separate.
Choose how long each stage gives someone to act. A stage’s clock starts only when that stage begins, and an expired deadline still needs a transaction to finish its timeout.
All four durations are required, from 1 second to the maximum shown above. Phases start at the successful transaction’s block time.

The acceptance period gives the contractor time to accept after the agreement is created. Before its deadline the client may also cancel; if acceptance remains pending at or after it, anyone can finalize the full escrow as client credit. Withdrawal is separate.

Work time begins when the contractor accepts. The contractor can submit evidence before the deadline; once it is reached, anyone can finalize a still-unsubmitted agreement as full client credit. The deadline does not finalize or withdraw funds by itself.

Review time begins when work evidence is submitted. The client can approve or dispute before the deadline; at or after it, anyone can finalize a pending review as full contractor credit. Neither finalization nor withdrawal happens automatically.

The arbitration period gives the named arbitrator time to decide a dispute. Before its deadline they may award the full escrow as credit to either party; at or after an unresolved deadline, anyone can finalize full credit to the fixed timeout recipient. Withdrawal is separate.
Starts at dispute.

This choice is the fallback outcome for an unresolved arbitration deadline. It names the client or contractor who receives full escrow credit when anyone finalizes that timeout. The client fixes it at creation, and the credit is withdrawn separately.
This choice cannot be changed later.
Use this to record which terms document the parties are working from. Its location and SHA-256 digest together let someone retrieve it and check for matching bytes.

Enter the agreed terms URI or embed a short document. Use a local file or a browser-readable URL to calculate SHA-256 from the exact document bytes; for embedded content, calculate it directly. You can also enter it manually. Local files are not uploaded or checked against the URI. Both fields are required; replace the all-zero placeholder.
Find an agreement using the account and exact agreement reference above.
No matching agreement is stored here. Check the exact ID and whether this is the escrow contract and network where it was created.

valueLabels.refunded.arbitratorToClient: Arbitrator decided for client; client credited

props.text: The state records the stage the agreement has reached. Check it together with the current deadline and available actions to see what can happen next.
When an agreement closes, its funds become credit for the client or contractor shown in Agreement status. That account must withdraw the credit separately.

props.label: Role of the address being viewed

props.text: Any account can finalize an expired deadline, including an account with no agreement role.

The client funds and reviews; the contractor accepts and submits work; the arbitrator can award disputed funds. Naming the arbitrator does not confirm their consent: there is no on-chain acceptance step.
The amount funded at creation, also shown after settlement.
For an active phase, ordinary phase actions stop at or after this deadline; finalizing its timeout still needs a transaction.
The client’s exact lookup reference; use it with the client address to find this agreement.

These durations were fixed at creation. Each phase starts when its preceding action succeeds: creation starts acceptance, acceptance starts work, submission starts review, and a dispute starts arbitration.

This choice is the fallback outcome for an unresolved arbitration deadline. It names the client or contractor who receives full escrow credit when anyone finalizes that timeout. The client fixes it at creation, and the credit is withdrawn separately.
This choice cannot be changed later.
Review the document references behind the agreement: terms from the client, submission from the contractor, and any dispute from the client. The recorded digest can be compared with a retrieved file.

An empty evidence URI and all-zero digest mean it has not been recorded. A URI locates a document; the digest is the party’s claimed SHA-256 fingerprint of its exact bytes. Retrieve the file independently and compare its SHA-256 to check for matching bytes. This view and the contract do not fetch or verify documents.
The agreement moves through acceptance, work and client review, with arbitration if disputed. Here you can inspect its record and use the actions currently available.
Settlement adds the full escrow to the recipient’s account credit. Withdrawing that credit is a separate transaction.

props.title: View and manage an escrow agreement

props.text: Use this view to inspect how the agreement ended. Settlement created credit for one party, while withdrawal of that credit happens separately.
This agreement is closed and has no further agreement-changing actions.
When credit is available, send the withdrawal transaction from the account shown. The withdrawal sends the full balance; partial withdrawals are unavailable.
No credit is available to withdraw.
When credit is available, send the withdrawal transaction from the account shown. The withdrawal sends the full balance; partial withdrawals are unavailable.

props.label: Find agreement by client and reference

props.text: Link the work evidence so the client can review it against the terms. The agreement stores the document reference and starts the review period when submission succeeds.

Enter the submission URI or embed a short document. The URI is limited to 512 UTF-8 bytes. Calculate SHA-256 from the exact file bytes or a browser-readable URL; for embedded content, calculate it directly. You can also enter the digest manually. Local files are not uploaded or checked against the URI. Both fields are required; replace the all-zero placeholder.
Record why the client disputes the submission and where the supporting evidence can be found. A successful dispute starts the arbitration period.

Enter the dispute URI or embed a short document. The URI is limited to 512 UTF-8 bytes. Calculate SHA-256 from the exact file bytes or a browser-readable URL; for embedded content, calculate it directly. You can also enter the digest manually. Local files are not uploaded or checked against the URI. Both fields are required; replace the all-zero placeholder.

props.label: Total withdrawable credit for this account

props.text: Settling an agreement records credit rather than sending money straight to a wallet. Here you can check that account’s remaining credit and prepare its withdrawal when available.
This total combines credit from all ended agreements in this escrow for the account being viewed, less previous withdrawals. It excludes funds still locked in open agreements.
Use an agreement ID to open one specific record directly. It is the long identifier copied from an agreement view, not the client’s own reference.
Enter 0x followed by 64 hexadecimal characters. Use the same escrow contract and network where the agreement was created.
Choose an address to receive the full withdrawal. It may differ from the credit owner, but only that owner can submit the withdrawal transaction.

The recipient defaults to the account being viewed. Enter 0x followed by 40 hexadecimal characters. The zero address and this escrow contract are rejected. The recipient must be able to receive this chain’s native asset.
The signing wallet becomes the client.
These agreement details were read at the estimate block and can change before confirmation.
The signing wallet’s entire available credit is sent to the recipient. The account being viewed can differ from the signing wallet; its credit is shown below and may change before confirmation.
